bib.title: DataSpace: Benchmarking Data Agents for Verifiable Analytics over Heterogeneous Workspaces

legacy_report:
COVERAGE: All 24 pages read (125,325 chars extracted, text clean). Appendices A.1-A.2 (prompt templates for translation) were skimmed; everything else read. Reference list skimmed. No embedded instructions found.

SOURCE: "DataSpace: Benchmarking Data Agents for Verifiable Analytics over Heterogeneous Workspaces". First author Boyan Li (HKUST(GZ), Guangzhou; equal contribution with Zhuowen Liang and Yupeng Xie). 14 authors; most are HKUST(GZ). Yuan Li and Guoliang Li are at Tsinghua University, Beijing. Senior authors: Nan Tang, Guoliang Li, Yuyu Luo. arXiv:2608.03451v1 [cs.AI], 4 Aug 2026. The venue is a "Conference'17" template placeholder, so treat it as preprint. It was the official benchmark of the KDD Cup 2026 "Data Agents for Complex Data Analysis". Code: github.com/HKUSTDial/DataSpace. Data: huggingface.co/datasets/HKUSTDial/DataSpace.

CORE CLAIM: Data-agent benchmarks rarely combine a heterogeneous workspace, a complete-table output contract, and deterministic scoring. DataSpace does all three. It has 410 tasks and 7,439 artifacts (15.01 GB) in CSV, JSON, SQLite, Markdown, PDF and video. The agent gets only a question and a workspace and returns a full CSV table. It is scored by a model-free evaluator (header-invariant column alignment, type- and precision-aware normalization, row order checked only when the task requires it). It is built from EHRSQL and BULL Text-to-SQL items (363 BULL, 47 EHRSQL) and checked by 11 experts. Gold answers come from SQL execution.

HEADLINE NUMBERS (all 410 tasks, binary exact-match Task Accuracy, no LLM judge)
1. Backbone comparison: a fixed ReAct agent (DataSpace-Agent: bash, view_image, submit_answer). Limits are 60 turns, 50 tool actions and 1,800 s per task, with 4 CPUs, 16 GiB and no network. Provider-default reasoning effort. Models were accessed in July 2026.
   - Grok 4.5: 272/410, 66.34%
   - GPT-5.6 Sol: 265, 64.63%
   - Kimi K3: 219, 53.41%
   - MiMo-V2.5: 161, 39.27%
   - Claude Sonnet 5: 135, 32.93%
   - MiniMax M3: 117, 28.54%
   - Of the six, 56 tasks are solved by all and 76 by none. The oracle union solves 334 (81.46%).
2. Harness comparison with MiMo-V2.5 fixed, each harness with its native loop and the same 1,800 s limit but no shared action cap:
   - Grok Build v0.2.106: 46.34%
   - Claude Code v2.1.217: 183, 44.63%
   - DataSpace-Agent: 161, 39.27%
   - Codex v0.145.0: 143, 34.88%
   - Smolagents v1.26.0: 127, 30.98%
   - The spread is 15.36 points.
3. Efficiency (DataSpace-Agent): GPT-5.6 Sol is 1.71 points below Grok 4.5 with 74.2% fewer tokens, 50.3% fewer actions and 39.2% less latency. Cost per task is $0.011 for MiMo-V2.5, $0.169 for Grok and $0.200 for GPT. For five of six backbones, a failed task uses 1.2 to 3.2 times the mean tokens of a solved one (GPT is the exception).
4. Degradation: multimodal tasks (134) score below single-modal tasks (276) for every backbone, by 1.8 to 14.0 points. Joins (113 tasks) cost 9.7 to 19.8 points. Language and answer shape effects vary by backbone.
5. Failure audit of the 136 Grok 4.5 failures: 71 (52.2%) are answer materialization and 31 (22.8%) are intent. Within those, 60 add or omit columns and 17 misstate output or row grain, which together make 77 (56.6%). Only 3 failures are the wrong evidence source. Of 74 column-count mismatches, 58 start in materialization. Of 13 no-submit outcomes, only 5 are pure termination failures.

QUOTES
- "harness choice creates a 15.36-point spread with the backbone fixed" (abstract, p.1)
- "Harnesses must faithfully materialize the exact requested output, rather than merely find and correctly compute the relevant values" (Finding 4, p.8)
- "Near-top accuracy need not require long trajectories" (Finding 2)

LIMITS / NOT SHOWN
- Each configuration appears to be a single run. I found no seeds, repeated runs, variance or confidence intervals, and no pass@k. The 1.71-point gap between Grok and GPT (7 tasks) is therefore not backed by any noise estimate.
- The stratified results (Fig. 6) are described by the authors as "descriptive rather than causal". The strata overlap.
- Harness results use only MiMo-V2.5, the weakest-but-one and a cheap open-weight model. Harness ranking may not transfer to stronger backbones.
- The harness comparison lets each harness keep its own action budget and context policy, so it is not a controlled comparison of the loops themselves.
- Tasks are synthetic: Text-to-SQL items rendered into files, documents and video by LLMs (Gemini 2.5 Pro, GPT-4o, Claude Sonnet 4.6, Qwen-Plus). The domains are only finance, macro and healthcare.
- Only 60 of 410 references are public, and the other 350 are withheld.
- The failure audit uses one model (Grok 4.5). GPT-5.6 Sol proposed the root causes and a human checked each one, so there is no inter-annotator agreement.
- Specialized data-agent systems (DeepAnalyze, AgenticData, TAIJI, AOP) were excluded as not runnable.
- Answer-format failures dominate. This partly measures the strict exact-schema contract rather than analytical ability (the paper itself concedes these are "distinct routes to an incorrect answer schema").
- The model names (Grok 4.5, GPT-5.6 Sol, Sonnet 5, etc.) are as printed in the paper. I did not verify them.

BUILDS ON: Spider (Yu et al.), BIRD (Li 2023), Spider 2.0 (Lei 2025), EHRSQL (Lee 2023), BULL, DABStep (Egg 2025), KramaBench (Lai 2025), LongDA (Li 2026), DataCross (Qi 2026), FDABench, MMLongBench-Doc (Ma 2024), ReAct (Yao 2022), DataMagic (for video rendering). It follows Data Agent Benchmark (Ma 2026) and AgenticDataBench (Sun 2026).

BEST-FIT NOTE SECTION: "Agent-specific suites" (line 371), as a new paragraph beside MedBrowseComp, NatureBench, AutoLab and LiveMCP-101. Secondary: "Grade the outcome by state, not by words" (line 106). The model-free canonicalizing evaluator, with its frozen per-task column types and precision, is a clean example of outcome grading. A third option is "Efficiency metrics" (line 301), for the accuracy-versus-tokens/cost trade-off.
What the note lacks, from the headings:
- Harness-versus-model variance: the same backbone moves 15.36 points across harnesses.
- Output-contract and materialization failures as a failure class. The audit finds 56.6% of failures are wrong schema, not wrong analysis.
- Symptom versus root cause in trace audits.
- Header-invariant table grading as a way to avoid an LLM judge.
- A caveat that single-run numbers are not k-run numbers. This contrasts with the note's "run every task k times" section.

FIGURE CANDIDATE: Figure 7 (p.8), the error-analysis bar and matrix of the 136 Grok 4.5 failures by stage (Q/D/E/G/C/M/T) against evaluator symptom. It shows that the symptom is not the cause. Alternative: Table 3 for the harness spread.
